arxiv-1712-06679.title: DecideNet: Counting Varying Density Crowds Through Attention Guided Detection and Density Estimation
arxiv-1712-06679.creator: Jiang Liu, Chenqiang Gao, Deyu Meng, Alexander G. Hauptmann
arxiv-1712-06679.description: Abstract In real-world crowd counting applications, the crowd densities vary greatly in spatial and temporal domains. A detection based counting method will estimate crowds accurately in low density scenes, while its reliability in congested areas is downgraded. A regression based approach, on the other hand, captures the general density information in crowded regions.

arxiv-2111-11363.creator: Jing Yang Lee 1 , Kong Aik Lee 2 and Woon Seng Gan 1 1 School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore 2 Institute for Infocomm Research, A*Star, Singapore jingyang001@e.ntu.edu.sg, kong_aik_lee@i2r.a-star.edu.sg, ewsgan@ntu.edu.sg

Typically, personalized dialogue generation models involve conditioning the generated response on the dialogue history and a representation of the persona/personality of the interlocutor.

arxiv-2304-01159.title: DribbleBot: Dynamic Legged Manipulation in the Wild
arxiv-2304-01159.creator: Yandong Ji, Gabriel B. Margolis, Pulkit Agrawal
arxiv-2304-01159.description: Abstract DribbleBot ( D exte r ous B all Manipulation with a Le gged Ro bot ) is a legged robotic system that can dribble a soccer ball under the same real-world conditions as humans (i.e., in-the-wild ). We adopt the paradigm of training policies in simulation using reinforcement learning and transferring them into the real world.

arxiv-2305-01499.title: GROUP-FRAMES FOR BANACH SPACES
arxiv-2305-01499.creator: K. MAHESH KRISHNA
arxiv-2305-01499.description: Abstract Abstract : In the literature, frames generated by unitary representations of groups (known as group-frames) are studied only for Hilbert spaces. We make first study of frames for Banach spaces generated by isometric invertible representations of discrete groups on Banach spaces. These frames are characterized using left regular, right regular, Gram-matrices and group-matrices on classical sequence spaces.

arxiv-2306-10771.title: Master Thesis - Paper
arxiv-2306-10771.creator: Laurin Felder
arxiv-2306-10771.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Laurin Felder. Matrix configurations define noncommutative spaces endowed with extra structure including a generalized Laplace operator, and hence a metric structure. Made dynamical via matrix models, they describe rich physical systems including noncommutative gauge theory and emergent gravity. Refining the construction in [ 1 ] , we construct a semi-classical limit through an immersed submanifold of complex projective space based on quasi-coherent states. We observe the phenomenon of oxidation, where the resulting semi-classical space acquires spurious extra dimensions.

arxiv-2307-14316.title: Reinforcement Learning by Guided Safe Exploration
arxiv-2307-14316.creator: Qisong Yang, Thiago D. Simão, Nils Jansen, Simon H. Tindemans, Matthijs T. J. Spaan
arxiv-2307-14316.description: Abstract Safety is critical to broadening the application of reinforcement learning (RL). Often, we train RL agents in a controlled environment, such as a laboratory, before deploying them in the real world. However, the real-world target task might be unknown prior to deployment. Reward-free RL trains an agent without the reward to adapt quickly once the reward is revealed.

arxiv-2406-00926.title: Quantum turbulence, superfluidity, non-Markovian dynamics, and wave function thermalization
arxiv-2406-00926.creator: Aurel Bulgac, Matthew Kafker, Ibrahim Abdurrahman, Gabriel Wlazłowski
arxiv-2406-00926.description: Abstract While quantum turbulence has been addressed both experimentally (predominantly for superfluid 4 He and 3 He) and theoretically, the dynamics of various ensembles of quantized vortices was followed in time only until the vortices decay into phonons. How this “thermalization” is achieved is still an unaddressed and thus an unelucidated question.

arxiv-2407-09083.title: BKDSNN: Enhancing the Performance of Learning-based Spiking Neural Networks Training with Blurred Knowledge Distillation
arxiv-2407-09083.creator: Zekai Xu, Kang You, Qinghai Guo, Xiang Wang, Zhezhi He
arxiv-2407-09083.description: Abstract Spiking neural networks (SNNs), which mimic biological neural systems to convey information via discrete spikes, are well-known as brain-inspired models with excellent computing efficiency. By utilizing the surrogate gradient estimation for discrete spikes, learning-based SNN training methods that can achieve ultra-low inference latency ( i.e . , number of time-step) have emerged recently.

arxiv-2409-20534.title: End-to-End Conformal Calibration for Optimization Under Uncertainty
arxiv-2409-20534.creator: Christopher Yeh cyeh@caltech.edu
arxiv-2409-20534.description: Abstract Machine learning can significantly improve performance for decision-making under uncertainty across a wide range of domains. However, ensuring robustness guarantees requires well-calibrated uncertainty estimates, which can be difficult to achieve with neural networks. Moreover, in high-dimensional settings, there may be many valid uncertainty estimates, each with its own performance profile—i.e., not all uncertainty is equally valuable for downstream decision-making.

arxiv-2411-18769.description: Abstract Photometric redshifts will be a key data product for the Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) as well as for future ground and space-based surveys. The need for photometric redshifts, or photo-zs, arises from sparse spectroscopic coverage of observed galaxies.
